technicalChanges.from: SSL compression enabled for eligible inter-instance traffic
technicalChanges.to: HTTP compression becomes the default, except for SSL forwarding
technicalChanges.implication: Mixed-version communications can negotiate different compression behavior, while forwarding remains an exception.
technicalChanges.action: Validate inter-instance communications and throughput assumptions, especially where SSL forwarding or older peers remain.

features: Route, filter, mask, and transform data on heavy forwarders before it reaches indexes.
Build federated searches with guided UI support across compatible Splunk environments.
Audit configuration changes and troubleshoot drift with clearer context.
Receive configuration insights and recommendations from a connected cloud service.

technicalChanges.from: Python 2 compatibility remains available
technicalChanges.to: Python 3-compatible code is required
technicalChanges.implication: Apps, scripted inputs, custom commands, and templates that still use Python 2 syntax can stop working.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory Python-dependent apps and scripts, update them for Python 3, and validate them before the platform upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB 3.6 with the MMAP storage engine
technicalChanges.to: MongoDB 4.2 with the WiredTiger storage engine
technicalChanges.implication: KV Store collections used by apps must move to the supported database and storage-engine baseline.
technicalChanges.action: Back up KV Store, complete the documented storage-engine and MongoDB migration, and validate dependent apps.

technicalChanges.from: Legacy journal compression and tsidx writing defaults
technicalChanges.to: zstd journal compression and tsidx writing level 3 by default
technicalChanges.implication: Newly written index artifacts use updated storage and search-performance optimizations.
technicalChanges.action: Benchmark representative indexing and search workloads and account for mixed-version behavior during staged upgrades.

technicalChanges.from: Deployment clients earlier than 7.0 can remain connected
technicalChanges.to: Version 7.0 or later is required with the hardened 9.0 deployment server
technicalChanges.implication: Older deployment clients can lose communication after the deployment-server security change.
technicalChanges.action: Identify clients earlier than 7.0, upgrade them, and review whether the deployment server must be isolated before upgrading.

requirements: Splunk Enterprise 9.0 moves KV Store from MongoDB 3.6 to 4.2. Complete the documented migration and validate apps that depend on KV Store.

technicalChanges.from: Older libraries remain broadly available
technicalChanges.to: Libraries older than jQuery 3.5 are restricted by default
technicalChanges.implication: Classic dashboards and custom apps that depend on older jQuery behavior can fail unless remediated or temporarily re-enabled.
technicalChanges.action: Run the jQuery Upgrade Readiness checks and migrate app JavaScript to supported APIs.

technicalChanges.from: Event format inferred from the destination log name
technicalChanges.to: The expected subscription format can be set with wec_event_format
technicalChanges.implication: Subscriptions using RenderedText outside the conventional ForwardedEvents naming pattern can otherwise be parsed incorrectly.
technicalChanges.action: Review Windows Event Collector subscriptions and explicitly set the format where destination naming does not convey it.

technicalChanges.from: New installations commonly use the splunk account
technicalChanges.to: The installer creates a least-privileged splunkfwd account
technicalChanges.implication: File ownership, protected-log access, service control, and deployment automation can depend on the operating-system identity.
technicalChanges.action: Validate permissions and installation automation for new or rebuilt Linux forwarders.

technicalChanges.from: The October 14 advance notice named 9.4.16 without CVE or affected-version detail
technicalChanges.to: SVD-2026-1007, -1008 and -1009 publish the October 21 vulnerability, hardening and third-party package fixes; 9.4.16 is the fixed 9.4 version
technicalChanges.implication: The definitive advisories establish affected versions and a Critical 9.9 hardening issue. They apply to customer-managed Splunk Enterprise and do not establish Splunk Cloud rollout, entitlement, region or authorization.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade maintained 9.4 deployments to 9.4.16 or later and review all three October 21 advisories for applicable component and package remediation.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise 9.4.0 through 9.4.15
technicalChanges.to: 9.4.16 or later
technicalChanges.implication: SVD-2026-1008 rates the disclosed hardening issue Critical, CVSS 9.9. This customer-managed Enterprise floor does not establish Cloud service remediation.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade maintained 9.4 deployments to 9.4.16 or later and retain the advisory in the security review record.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise 9.4.0 through 9.4.15
technicalChanges.to: 9.4.16 or later with the SVD-2026-1009 package updates
technicalChanges.implication: The package advisory has component-specific applicability; it is not evidence for Cloud rollout or an independently installed package outside the listed Enterprise distribution.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade the affected Enterprise package and verify the advisory's applicable dependency rows in the deployment inventory.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise 9.4.0 through 9.4.15
technicalChanges.to: 9.4.16 is the October 21 fixed version
technicalChanges.implication: The October 21 Enterprise advisories supersede the earlier 9.4.15 floor and include vulnerability-, hardening- and package-specific remediation. Selecting the 9.4 line alone does not establish a safe patch.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade maintained 9.4 deployments to 9.4.16 or later, review SVD-2026-1007, -1008 and -1009, and validate the exact maintenance build before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB 4.2 or later
technicalChanges.to: MongoDB 7.0 becomes the preferred and automatically upgraded engine
technicalChanges.implication: The newer engine changes the supported host baseline and the database version used for app collections.
technicalChanges.action: Back up KV Store, ensure the existing engine is at least 4.2, verify host processor support, and validate collections after migration.

technicalChanges.from: Older x86-64 processors may remain usable
technicalChanges.to: AVX, SSE4.2, and AES-NI support is required for the KV Store 7 baseline
technicalChanges.implication: Unsupported processors can prevent Splunk Enterprise from running or cause an upgrade to fail.
technicalChanges.action: Verify every physical and virtual host exposes the required CPU instructions before scheduling the upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: Admins can temporarily re-enable older jQuery libraries
technicalChanges.to: Older-library controls and the Internal Library Settings page are removed
technicalChanges.implication: The self-service compatibility escape hatch for older app and dashboard JavaScript is no longer available.
technicalChanges.action: Remediate apps and dashboards that use unsupported or hot-linked libraries before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: web.conf and restmap.conf are treated as externally controlled static files
technicalChanges.to: Splunk sidecars can update both files dynamically under system/local
technicalChanges.implication: Configuration-management tools that automatically revert these writes can trigger instability or restart loops.
technicalChanges.action: Allow Splunk-managed portions of these files to change asynchronously and test configuration-management reconciliation.

requirements: Splunk identifies 9.4.0 through 9.4.15 as affected and 9.4.16 as the fixed version. Upgrade to 9.4.16 or later and complete the applicable vulnerability, hardening and third-party package remediation in SVD-2026-1007, -1008 and -1009.
Hosts require AVX, SSE4.2, and AES-NI processor support. Verify every target hostâ€”not only a representative node.

technicalChanges.to: A more reliable checkpoint backend writes new file-monitoring state

technicalChanges.from: Older Linux distributions may host Edge Processor
technicalChanges.to: Security updates require a currently supported Linux distribution
technicalChanges.implication: Unsupported Edge Processor hosts can crash after the control plane upgrade and cause data loss.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade every affected management and Edge Processor host operating system before moving the control plane to 10.2.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.2
technicalChanges.to: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.4 is the current maintenance release and October 21 fixed version
technicalChanges.implication: Version 10.4.2 can block tcpout forwarding pipelines when acknowledgements are enabled, and the October 21 advisories now identify 10.4.0 through 10.4.3 as affected. The earlier 10.4.3 operational floor is no longer a security-safe fallback.
technicalChanges.action: Target 10.4.4 or later for new upgrade work, do not use 10.4.2, and validate acknowledged forwarding plus the applicable October advisory actions before production rollout.

technicalChanges.from: splunkd uses Python 3.9 by default with Python 3.13 opt-in; Splunk Web already uses Python 3.13
technicalChanges.to: Python 3.13 becomes the default interpreter with Python 3.9 available as a fallback
technicalChanges.implication: Private apps, custom search commands, REST endpoints, scripted or modular inputs, and packaged libraries can expose Python-version assumptions when the default changes.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory Python-dependent extensions, confirm supported app releases, and test representative workflows with the 3.13 default before production rollout.

technicalChanges.from: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated but available
technicalChanges.to: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 support is completely removed
technicalChanges.implication: Splunk component and integration connections using a legacy protocol can no longer negotiate successfully.
technicalChanges.action: Move every endpoint to TLS 1.2 or later and validate the complete trust path before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: SHA-1-signed certificates are deprecated
technicalChanges.to: SHA-1 certificate signatures are rejected; SHA-256 or stronger is required
technicalChanges.implication: Internal and external connections can fail even when the protocol version itself is acceptable.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory and reissue SHA-1-signed certificates, then validate trust chains and mutual-authentication paths.

technicalChanges.from: Install media retains older MongoDB engine binaries
technicalChanges.to: Unsupported MongoDB binaries are removed; engine 7 or later is required
technicalChanges.implication: A deployment still using an older KV Store engine cannot rely on the 10.4 package to perform that older transition.
technicalChanges.action: Upgrade KV Store to MongoDB engine 7 or later and verify app collections before starting the 10.4 upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB 7 is the supported pre-upgrade KV Store baseline
technicalChanges.to: MongoDB 8.0, upgraded automatically from a supported 10.x path
technicalChanges.implication: MongoDB 4.x and 6.x cannot move directly to the 10.4 engine, so older deployments need a supported bridge release and a validated KV Store backup.
technicalChanges.action: Reach the documented MongoDB 7 floor before 10.4, retain a validated KV Store backup, and verify app collections after the automatic engine upgrade.

technicalChanges.from: Overlapping kvstore settings can be ignored in favor of sslConfig
technicalChanges.to: TLS settings in the kvstore stanza take precedence
technicalChanges.implication: Conflicting protocol settings can produce unexpected KV Store connection failures after the upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Compare both server.conf stanzas and remove unused or conflicting TLS settings before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Enterprise can run under an administrator-level account
technicalChanges.to: Local service or non-administrator domain accounts are required
technicalChanges.implication: The installer can reconfigure a local-system deployment or halt when a domain service account remains an administrator.
technicalChanges.action: Choose and validate the target service account, file permissions, service control, and domain policy before upgrading.

technicalChanges.from: jQuery 2 compatibility artifacts can remain
technicalChanges.to: jQuery 2, related feature flags, and the quarantine framework are removed
technicalChanges.implication: Apps that hotlink jQuery 2 or depend on version-specific APIs no longer function.
technicalChanges.action: Run AppInspect, migrate classic dashboards where required, and move custom JavaScript to jQuery 3-compatible APIs.

requirements: Splunk identifies 10.4.0 through 10.4.3 as affected and 10.4.4 as the fixed version. Upgrade to 10.4.4 or later and complete applicable component-specific remediation, including the documented Edge Processor package-download authentication and restart sequence when that path is used.

Splunk Enterprise 10.4.4 is the current published maintenance release and the October 21 fixed version. Do not use 10.4.2 because tcpout with useACK=true can block forwarding pipelines, and do not treat 10.4.3 as a security-safe fallback because SVD-2026-1007 identifies it as affected.
All deployments must use KV Store 7. Complete the migration and verify app collections before moving to 10.4.
TLS 1.0/1.1 and SHA-1-signed certificates are removed. Inventory every internal and external connection and replace incompatible endpoints.
Root and administrator service identities are no longer supported. Confirm file ownership, ports, boot configuration, and service accounts.
Run AppInspect, remove jQuery 2 dependencies, and plan migration for classic Simple XML dashboards affected by current lifecycle guidance.
The auto_refresh_dashboards capability governs automatic dashboard refresh. Confirm roles retain intended behavior.

Validate provider versions and connectivity with stronger preflight checks.
Accommodate the new four-segment version format in inventory, automation, and policy logic.
Use the newly certified Universal Forwarder line after validating its distinct upgrade, OS, and receiver evidence.

technicalChanges.from: The versioned page did not expose an explicit 10.6 upgrade-path table
technicalChanges.to: The published table names supported 10.6 paths from 9.4.x, 10.0.x, 10.2.x and 10.4.x
technicalChanges.implication: Enterprise and Heavy Forwarder planning can use the documented release-line edges, while exact maintenance, app, OS, topology and receiver checks remain separate.
technicalChanges.action: Use 10.0.x or 10.2.x as the first step from 9.4.x; 10.0.x, 10.2.x and 10.4.x can then move to 10.6.x as listed. Validate exact maintenance releases before execution.

technicalChanges.from: MongoDB-backed KV Store
technicalChanges.to: Cohosted PostgreSQL KV Store begins in 10.6
technicalChanges.implication: Migration starts automatically unless postponed. KV Store writes are impaired during migration; the current guide requires ITSI 5.0.x and lower to postpone and separately describes degraded premium-app functionality during migration. ES incompatibility remains a separate matrix warning.
technicalChanges.action: Verify KV Store 7.0+, more than 50% free disk space, healthy cluster and parallel backup. For ITSI 5.0.x and lower, set postgresMigrateOnStartup=false before upgrading and verify every member; also retain the separate ES matrix warning.

technicalChanges.from: The general Enterprise 10.6 upgrade table lists a direct path from 10.0.x
technicalChanges.to: The KV Store guide requires Enterprise 10.2 or higher first when starting at 10.0 or lower
technicalChanges.implication: General release-line upgrade support does not settle the KV Store prerequisite. The two published instructions differ for a direct 10.0-to-10.6 move with KV Store.
technicalChanges.action: For KV Store deployments starting at 10.0 or lower, use the documented 10.2-or-higher bridge and verify KV Store 7.0+; retain the general table separately and seek authoritative scope clarification before relying on its direct 10.0 path.

technicalChanges.from: Earlier documentation differs on removal versus temporary enablement
technicalChanges.to: 10.6 disallows TLS 1.0/1.1 for inter-Splunk connections; no temporary override
technicalChanges.implication: Connections still requiring legacy TLS cannot be restored with the earlier temporary switch.
technicalChanges.action: Validate TLS 1.2 or 1.3 on each inter-Splunk connection before upgrading. The unresolved 10.4 timing conflict remains separate.

technicalChanges.from: Remote providers can run older Enterprise release lines
technicalChanges.to: Remote Splunk Enterprise providers must be 10.4 or later
technicalChanges.implication: A 10.6 search head cannot rely on older remote providers for a supported federated-search topology.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory every remote provider and upgrade any provider below 10.4 before moving the federated-search head to 10.6.

technicalChanges.from: Some public certificates include both serverAuth and clientAuth EKUs
technicalChanges.to: Public issuers are expected to stop issuing dual-use certificates by March 1, 2027
technicalChanges.implication: Using a server-only public certificate for mutual TLS or KV Store client authentication can cause service disruption after renewal.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory certificates by component. Keep Splunk Web certificates serverAuth-only and use a suitable private PKI or client-auth chain for mutual-TLS and KV Store component certificates.

technicalChanges.from: Three-segment release identifiers
technicalChanges.to: Four-segment release identifiers can be published
technicalChanges.implication: Strict parsers, deployment rules, CMDB fields, and comparison scripts can reject or misorder valid releases.
technicalChanges.action: Test version parsing and ordering in automation, deployment tooling, reports, and asset inventories.

technicalChanges.from: Supported custom visualizations in Classic dashboards
technicalChanges.to: Custom Visualizations support in Classic dashboards is deprecated
technicalChanges.implication: Existing dashboards are not described as removed in 10.6, but new investment increases future migration risk.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory affected Classic dashboards and plan supported replacements without treating deprecation as immediate removal.

technicalChanges.from: The platform pairing alone does not establish database-engine compatibility

approaches.title: Greenfield
approaches.fit: Best when historical data can remain behind or age out and the priority is a clean, no-outage cutover.
strengths: Easy to align to current best practices
approaches.tradeoff: Historical data is not copied, and load testing is limited before redirection.

approaches.title: Dual running
approaches.fit: Best when the target must be validated with real production load and data can be sent to both environments temporarily.
strengths: Historical access can age out naturally
approaches.tradeoff: Requires parallel capacity and usually creates the longest migration window.

approaches.title: Full migration
approaches.fit: Best when historical data must move and the on-premises environment has a firm retirement deadline.
approaches.tradeoff: Requires an outage sized to data volume and offers the least forgiving rollback path.

technicalChanges.action: Test the same service with the intended declarative file and environment variables, verify effective resources and trace-response-header behavior, and keep profiling and callgraph variables explicit until Splunk documents declarative equivalents.

technicalChanges.from: Generated distribution metadata advertises SPLUNK_OTEL_SYSTEM_METRICS_ENABLED even though the runtime does not read it
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 removes the unsupported variable from generated metadata; system metrics remain enabled through auto-instrumentation and can be disabled with OTEL_PYTHON_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=system_metrics
technicalChanges.implication: Deployments that set the obsolete variable never controlled runtime system metrics, so retaining it can create a false belief that collection is disabled.
technicalChanges.action: Remove the ineffective setting from templates and use the documented disabled-instrumentations value when system metrics must be turned off; no runtime behavior change is implied by the metadata correction itself.

technicalChanges.from: Published Python init images target AMD64
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 publishes AMD64 and ARM64 variants for both standard and SecureApp init images
technicalChanges.implication: ARM64 Kubernetes workloads can use a matching init image instead of relying on an incompatible architecture, while standard and SecureApp images remain distinct deployment choices.
technicalChanges.action: Select the exact standard or SecureApp image for the workload, pin the intended 2.13.0 tag or digest, and validate injection and startup on representative ARM64 nodes before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: The distribution permits wrapt 2.2.2 or later
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.0 requires wrapt 2.5.0 or later
technicalChanges.implication: Application lock files, constraints, or base images pinned below wrapt 2.5.0 can conflict with installation or produce a different resolved environment during the agent upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Resolve the 2.13.0 agent in the application's locked dependency set, rebuild the deployment artifact, and run instrumentation smoke tests before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk OpenTelemetry Python 2.13.0
technicalChanges.to: Version 2.13.1 adopts the corresponding upstream OpenTelemetry Python patch release
technicalChanges.implication: The latest patch changes the upstream runtime baseline without adding a separately declared Splunk capability; the 2.13.0 configuration, dependency, and image qualifications still apply.
technicalChanges.action: Use 2.13.1 for the 2.13 line, retain the documented 2.13.0 rollout checks, and run representative instrumentation smoke tests against the resolved application dependencies.

technicalChanges.from: Rage clicks enabled by default, a five-second page-completion quiet window, and 2 MB localStorage retry persistence
technicalChanges.to: Four frustration signals enabled, a one-second quiet window, and up to 100 MB IndexedDB persistence for failed Session Replay uploads
technicalChanges.implication: Interaction volume, Page Completion Time baselines, client storage, privacy review, and replay retry behavior can differ without an application-code change.
technicalChanges.action: Review consent and storage policy, compare Page Completion Time baselines, and explicitly retain or disable earlier behaviors where the application requires them.

technicalChanges.from: spaMetrics is the configuration name used for single-page application navigation and page-completion settings
technicalChanges.to: Browser RUM 3.2 renames the configuration to navigationMetrics; spaMetrics remains supported as a deprecated alias
technicalChanges.implication: Existing deployments continue to work, but leaving the alias in templates or generated configuration creates future removal debt and can obscure where new manual page-load and blocking-element settings belong.
technicalChanges.action: Use navigationMetrics in new configuration, migrate maintained templates from spaMetrics during the normal rollout, and validate manual page-load registrations against the default 180-second maximum wait when adopted.

technicalChanges.from: Chart 0.163.0 packages Collector 0.163.0, Operator 0.126.0 and Target Allocator 0.161.1
technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.163.1 packages Collector 0.163.1, Operator 0.126.1, Target Allocator 0.161.2 and OBI 0.15.2

technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.163.0 enables k8s.persistentvolume.status.phase, k8s.persistentvolume.storage.capacity, k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.status.phase, k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.storage.capacity and k8s.persistentvolumeclaim.storage.request
technicalChanges.implication: With Observability metrics enabled, default cluster-metric collection can add storage telemetry; custom metrics and receiver overrides still require review.
technicalChanges.action: Compare the rendered cluster-receiver configuration and expected metric volume before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Earlier chart pipelines do not add transform/limit_histogram_buckets
technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.163.0 merges histogram buckets as needed to the 32-bucket ingest limit: agent control-plane pipeline with useControlPlaneMetricsHistogramData and metrics enabled; EKS API-server pipeline with enableEKSApiServerMetrics and Observability metrics enabled
technicalChanges.implication: Affected histogram bucket boundaries can change. Both gates default to true in this tag, but a disabled gate, pipeline or non-EKS distribution does not acquire the corresponding pipeline behavior.
technicalChanges.action: Inspect the rendered pipeline and bucket-dependent queries; do not apply this rule to every histogram or distribution.

technicalChanges.from: A != filter can retain data that does not contain the selected tag
technicalChanges.to: A != filter excludes data when the selected tag is absent
technicalChanges.implication: Saved searches, dashboards, detectors, links, and runbooks that rely on the earlier missing-tag behavior can return fewer results and change operational conclusions.
technicalChanges.action: Inventory APM searches that use !=, compare representative results, and add explicit missing-tag handling where the intended population includes data without the tag.

technicalChanges.from: Package exclusions apply globally across call graphs
technicalChanges.to: Package exclusions can be configured for individual applications
technicalChanges.implication: An application-specific exclusion can change call-graph shape without changing another application's graph. Existing global exclusions do not establish the intended per-application result.
technicalChanges.action: Review global exclusions, define application-specific exceptions deliberately and compare representative call graphs before broad use.

technicalChanges.from: When the Controlled Availability feature is enabled, Monitoring MetricSets are created for parentless spans with span.kind SERVER or CONSUMER
technicalChanges.to: When enabled, Monitoring MetricSets are created for parentless spans of any span.kind
technicalChanges.implication: Metric values, charts and detectors can change, and the additional time series can increase cardinality. The behavior remains Controlled Availability and is not inferred for every realm or tenant.
technicalChanges.action: Confirm feature access, baseline MetricSet values and cardinality, and validate affected charts and detectors before relying on the expanded coverage.

technicalChanges.from: Splunk Java instrumentation 2.33.0 with OpenTelemetry Java instrumentation 2.33.0
technicalChanges.to: Splunk Java instrumentation 2.33.1 with OpenTelemetry Java instrumentation 2.33.1
technicalChanges.implication: The customer-managed agent follows the upstream Java instrumentation patch. The release does not claim a new SaaS capability or selected-tenant rollout.
technicalChanges.action: Validate representative traces, call graphs, profiling controls, and agent/image packaging before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Node.js instrumentation 4.12.0 can repeatedly allocate profiler arena pages across resets
technicalChanges.to: Node.js instrumentation 4.12.1 retains and reuses arena pages and refreshes listed runtime dependencies
technicalChanges.implication: Long-running native-profiling processes can avoid the documented potential memory growth, while the dependency refresh still warrants normal patch validation.
technicalChanges.action: Monitor representative profiler memory behavior and validate tracing plus dependency compatibility before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: Chart 0.162.0 still accepts featureGates.useLightPrometheusReceiver after its earlier deprecation
technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.162.1 removes the Light Prometheus Receiver and its feature gate; autodetected Prometheus endpoints always use the standard Prometheus receiver
technicalChanges.implication: A values file that still relies on the removed gate no longer controls receiver selection, and resource use or collection behavior can change with the standard receiver.
technicalChanges.action: Remove the obsolete feature gate, compare representative endpoint discovery, collection completeness and resource use, and update operating thresholds before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: The prior chart packages an earlier OpAMP Bridge without the new cluster-ID-based standalone-agent identity path
technicalChanges.to: Chart 0.162.1 updates the OpAMP Bridge image to 0.161.0 and grants it read access to the kube-system namespace so the Kubernetes cluster ID can produce unique standalone-agent instance IDs
technicalChanges.implication: Restricted clusters can block the new lookup, while management views can identify standalone agents differently after the patch.
technicalChanges.action: Review the added namespace permission, validate bridge startup and cluster-ID resolution, and confirm expected standalone-agent identity continuity in Fleet Management.

technicalChanges.from: Python instrumentation 2.13.1 uses the preceding OpAMP client and a direct requests-dependency workaround
technicalChanges.to: Python instrumentation 2.13.2 uses OpAMP client 0.4b0 and removes the direct requests workaround
technicalChanges.implication: Remote-management initialization and resolved dependency behavior can change even though the patch does not declare a new instrumentation capability.
technicalChanges.action: Resolve dependencies in the target environment and validate startup, configuration delivery, traces, profiling and call graphs before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.component: Python 2.13.3 auto-instrumentation images and dependency floors
technicalChanges.from: Python instrumentation 2.13.2 retains the preceding auto-instrumentation image dependency layout and dependency floors
technicalChanges.to: Python instrumentation 2.13.3 bundles dependencies for CPython 3.10 through 3.14 in standard and SecureApp AMD64/ARM64 images, signs and verifies both variants, requires Requests 2.33.0+ and wrapt 2.5.1+, and loads declarative-configuration dependencies only when file configuration is used
technicalChanges.implication: The patch repairs documented image startup behavior and strengthens release integrity, but dependency resolution, architecture-specific image selection and declarative configuration startup can still change in a customer-managed deployment.
technicalChanges.action: Resolve the new dependency floors, verify the exact signed image and architecture, and test startup, declarative configuration, traces, profiling and call graphs before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.from: The maintained Python 2.13.2 baseline does not declare PostgreSQL query-to-trace correlation
technicalChanges.to: Python instrumentation 2.13.3 adds PostgreSQL query-to-trace correlation
technicalChanges.implication: PostgreSQL spans can gain correlation context after the agent patch; this component capability does not establish a rolling-service feature, tenant rollout or application-wide compatibility.
technicalChanges.action: Validate representative PostgreSQL traces, query attribution, data volume and sensitive-data handling before relying on the new correlation in production.

technicalChanges.from: Earlier distributions support Debian 11, the cook feature gate and the deprecated SignalFx Gateway Prometheus remote write receiver
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163 drops Debian 11 support, removes cook and removes signalfxgatewayprometheusremotewrite
technicalChanges.implication: Unsupported hosts and removed component declarations can prevent a working collection deployment. splunk_* receivers always apply props.conf but remain gated by enableTARunner.
technicalChanges.action: Migrate affected Debian hosts to a separately supported OS, remove +cook and replace the removed receiver with a documented supported pipeline; validate configuration and telemetry before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: prometheus_simple accepts deprecated tls_enabled and tls_config alongside tls
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163 removes tls_enabled and tls_config; use the standard tls block
technicalChanges.implication: Legacy TLS declarations no longer configure the receiver. Certificate validation and trust must survive the migration.
technicalChanges.action: Move ca_file, cert_file, key_file and applicable validation settings under tls; validate authenticated collection without weakening TLS.

technicalChanges.component: Collector 0.163 metric and database resource identity
technicalChanges.from: The SignalFx exporter emits container_cpu_utilization; database receivers use their earlier labels and aggregate series
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163 excludes generated container_cpu_utilization by default in favor of container.cpu.usage; MongoDB loopback server.address/service.instance.id change and server.port becomes enabled; direct SQL Server counters gain sqlserver.database.name and lose the unlabeled total
technicalChanges.implication: Queries, dashboards, detectors and series cardinality can change. These are Collector receiver/exporter contracts, not a Cloud Platform or tenant version.
technicalChanges.action: Rebaseline affected metrics and resource identity; explicitly include container_cpu_utilization only when required, aggregate SQL Server counters across the database attribute, and verify alert continuity.

technicalChanges.from: PostgreSQL receiver scrapes can remain unbounded
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163 defaults PostgreSQL scrape timeout to 60 seconds
technicalChanges.implication: Slow or blocked queries now terminate at the configured timeout and may alter collection completeness.
technicalChanges.action: Measure representative scrape durations and increase timeout when justified; timeout: 0 explicitly restores unbounded behavior.

technicalChanges.from: Chained redaction processors can delete, mask or double-count summary bookkeeping inconsistently
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163 preserves and accumulates owned summary attributes, but a downstream processor with summary unset or silent applies its ordinary allow list and can strip upstream summaries
technicalChanges.implication: An existing chained pipeline can lose audit summaries or handle body keys differently. No privacy guarantee follows from a version upgrade.
technicalChanges.action: Test chained redaction with representative non-sensitive fixtures and explicit summary/allowed_keys policy; verify both protected values and the intended audit trail before rollout.

technicalChanges.from: The receiver type is sqlserver
technicalChanges.to: The preferred type is sql_server; sqlserver remains a deprecated alias
technicalChanges.implication: Existing sqlserver configuration remains functional; deprecation is not removal or a mandatory immediate migration.
technicalChanges.action: Use sql_server in new configuration and plan maintained-template migration before any separately announced removal.

technicalChanges.from: The deprecated lightprometheus receiver remains available in standalone Collector 0.163.0
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163.1 removes lightprometheus; use prometheus or prometheus_simple
technicalChanges.implication: A configuration that still declares lightprometheus no longer has a valid receiver after the patch. The earlier chart-level removal and this standalone Collector removal are distinct package boundaries.
technicalChanges.action: Replace the receiver, compare discovery, scrape completeness and resource use, then validate the exact standalone or chart package actually deployed.

technicalChanges.from: The Splunk Connect for OpenTelemetry path can ignore configured source/sourcetype or token default index, reject every explicit index for unrestricted tokens, retry permanent authorization failures and permit a span index to bypass a denied resource index
technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163.1 applies HEC metadata/default-index behavior, treats denied indexes as permanent errors and prevents the span-index bypass; the new splunk_modinput exporter writes newline-delimited HEC JSON to stdout but does not perform index authorization
technicalChanges.implication: Output identity, retry behavior and accepted indexes can change. Using splunk_modinput does not inherit the Splunk OTLP input's token-index authorization checks.
technicalChanges.action: Patch the affected Collector path, test allowed and denied resource/span indexes, confirm default-index and metadata behavior, and enforce authorization at the correct input boundary when using splunk_modinput.

technicalChanges.component: Collector 0.163.1 Go and CA security refresh

technicalChanges.to: Collector 0.163.1 uses Go 1.26.10 and refreshed container CA certificates to mitigate CVE-2026-111943 and block trust in affected CA certificates

technicalChanges.action: Prioritize the patch for affected standalone deployments and validate required private/public trust chains plus telemetry delivery before broad rollout.

technicalChanges.implication: The bridge updates ConfigMaps and restarts enabled agent, gateway and cluster-receiver workloads. This is not automatic enrollment, universal entitlement or regulated-environment authorization.
technicalChanges.action: Confirm realm, access token and permissions; enable remoteManagement.enabled=true deliberately, test group/template assignment and validate controlled workload rollouts.

technicalChanges.implication: A documented feature announcement does not establish access for a particular account or realm. Search execution also depends on connected log data and notification configuration.
technicalChanges.action: Confirm account and realm access, validate the scheduled SPL search and event preview, then test firing, clearing and notifications before operational reliance.

baseline.action: Inventory admission, placement and monitoring rules; validate which controls work in the chosen current lab topology before assuming equivalent behavior.
